_comment: ENF-1. `families` are the model.schema.json $defs whose every property is a tracked keyword `<def>.<property>`.
A keyword is WITNESSED by a probe naming it in its own `keywords` array (NPDevSamples/dsl-conformance-max/behavior-probes/*.json);
this file never repeats that. A keyword with no probe must sit in an `allowlist` group with a reason and an open ledger id.
frozenCount pins the number of allowlisted keywords: it may only shrink, and lowering it is part of the same commit as the probe that removes an entry.
Checked by scripts/quality/check-dsl-behavior-witness.py (aiKnowledge gate); the probes run in scripts/quality/run-behavior-probes.ps1.

allowlist.reason: Structural container or identity key: a concept, flow, query or field cannot exist without it, so a runtime that ignored it would fail every probe at once; there is no separate behaviour to witness.

Identity, authoring or migration metadata (uid, metadata, renamedFrom, module, satelliteOf, specializes): consumed by tooling and the migrator, with no behaviour observable through the running app's REST API.
Presentation only (labels, help text, pickers, icons): rendered by the browser shell and covered by the browser scenarios, not by REST behaviour.

No model in the corpus declares it, so there is nothing to probe. Add a real example to dsl-conformance-max first (each enumOption property, each domainType validation/normalization/format, array-field limits, the extra invariant forms), then a probe. field.domainType is in this group because the only domain type (Sku) declares no validation or normalization, so the runtime accepts any value and there is nothing enforceable to assert.
The model declares no top-level seeds, so seed.* has no corpus example to probe; add a seeds example to dsl-conformance-max first.

Declared by no query / lifecycle state / transition / rule / action in the corpus (permissionRequirements, tracePolicy, terminal, allowedActions, guard, event, requires, requiredPayload, rule condition, delay and concept/event action variants); add a fixture example first.
File fields are enforced by the multipart upload endpoint (POST /api/files/{concept}/{field}), which the JSON probe runner cannot send; needs a multipart step type in run_probes.py.
Applies only to external-AI review packs, not to an ordinary concept read or write.

Needs a second principal: the API key always resolves to actor developer with role ADMIN and extra identity headers are ignored, so another role cannot be acted as (human-task outcomes need WarehouseManager; role grants need a non-admin caller). Needs a JWT-mode fixture or a second API key.

Schedules and timers have no REST-observable effect in this app: /api/admin/cron-schedules is 404 here, the only scheduled flow is a daily 03:15 six-field cron, timeouts are days. A probe needs a per-minute scheduled flow plus the SUPERUSER cron-schedules endpoint (the unit tests NpdevCronSchedulerServiceFiveFieldTest and CronSchedules.normalize cover the five-field case meanwhile).

Two declared forms are indistinguishable from outside in the current fixture (pre and post checkpoint share one condition; the only else arm sits after a failing step and both arms write the same variable).
Environment-bound: the orchestration rule's webhook target is not served in the probe environment, so the action outcome (capability, operation, map, action) cannot be asserted.

Not yet probed (work remaining for ENF-1): aggregate onValidate, collection concept/orderBy/ownership/via, concept events, and the flow-level and step-level action/data/concept fields have no distinct observable behaviour identified yet.
